results.name: chandra-ocr
results.title: Chandra OCR
results.summary: Chandra OCR 2 is a vision-language model for document parsing that converts images and PDFs into structured Markdown/HTML/JSON while preserving layout, with strength on math, tables, forms, handwriting, and 90+ languages; code is Apache-2.0, model weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M license

results.name: paddleocr
results.title: PaddleOCR
results.summary: PaddleOCR provides three product lines for document understanding — PP-OCRv6 scene text recognition, PP-StructureV3 document-structure-to-Markdown/JSON conversion, and the PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B-parameter vision-language model for full document parsing across 109 languages

results.name: ovisocr2
results.title: OvisOCR2
results.summary: Compact 0.8B-parameter vision-language model for end-to-end page-level document parsing — given a document page image, generates a single structured Markdown document (plain text, LaTeX formulas, HTML tables, and visual regions in natural reading order) without a multi-stage OCR pipeline; scores 96.58 overall on OmniDocBench v1.6 and 75.06 Avg3 on PureDocBench per the publisher's technical report

results.name: amazon-textract-textractor
results.title: Amazon Textract Textractor
results.summary: Textractor is a Python wrapper around Amazon Textract for document intelligence — handles API calls, response parsing, and output formatting for text recognition, table extraction, form extraction, ID analysis, and expense processing

results.name: olmocr
results.title: olmOCR
results.summary: AI2's VLM-based PDF/image-to-Markdown toolkit — 7B parameter model converts PDFs with equations, tables, handwriting, multi-column layouts into clean Markdown; <$200/M pages; multi-node S3-coordinated batch pipeline; ships comprehensive benchmark (7K+ test cases); Apache 2.0

results.name: jina-ocr-v1
results.title: Jina-OCR-v1
results.summary: End-to-end document-to-Markdown OCR model (3.4B total / 570M active MoE) with FastMTP speculative decoding (K=3, ~2x decode speed on L4) — scores 91.14 OmniDocBench, 83.4 olmOCR-Bench, 2.57 pages/s on A100; handles text, tables, math, handwriting, 100+ languages; runs via Transformers or vLLM; hosted via Jina Reader API; CC BY-NC 4.0 (weights)

results.name: tesseract
results.title: Tesseract OCR
results.summary: Open-source OCR engine (`libtesseract`) and CLI (`tesseract`), originally developed at HP and later Google, now maintained by Stefan Weil and Zdenko Podobny — LSTM-based neural line recognition in v4+ with the legacy v3 pattern-matching engine retained for compatibility, 100+ languages with UTF-8 output in plain text/hOCR/PDF/TSV/ALTO/PAGE formats; ~77.2k stars.

results.name: extractbench
results.title: ExtractBench
results.summary: ExtractBench evaluates document extraction systems on 370 enterprise-grade documents across 67 document types and 8 business domains, scoring schema-valid JSON output with a deterministic unified value F1 metric and no LLM-as-judge

results.name: armorocr
results.title: ArmorOCR
results.summary: Two-stage adversarial OCR framework built on Qwen3-VL-8B — trains robust grounded text perception via on-policy self-distillation from transformed observations, then refines with GRPO and task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, spotting, and VQA; includes AdvSpot benchmark (390 images, 13 adversarial OCR types)

results.name: liteparse
results.title: LiteParse
results.summary: Open-source, local-first document parser from the LlamaIndex team (`@llamaindex/liteparse`, PyPI `liteparse`, crates.io `liteparse`) — PDFium-based native text extraction in ~2-5ms/page when a document already has selectable text, bundled Tesseract OCR fallback (or a pluggable HTTP OCR backend) for scanned pages, and a per-page `is-complex`/needs_ocr check for routing decisions; Rust core with Node.js, Python, and WASM bindings plus a `lit` CLI; ~12.9k stars.

results.name: penecho
results.title: PenEcho
results.summary: Local-first AI canvas: put a question, equation, diagram, or half-formed idea anywhere on an infinite canvas and PenEcho reads the marks and their spatial relationships and answers beside them. Node server + browser UI; pluggable LLM source (Claude CLI, Codex CLI, Kimi CLI, or OpenAI/Anthropic API). A Kimi Open Source Friend. AGPL-3.0-only.

results.name: automate-the-boring-stuff
results.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
results.summary: Al Sweigart's beginner Python book (fully revised 3rd edition), free to read online under a Creative Commons license: teaches Python fundamentals then practical automation — file/folder operations, regex, web scraping, Excel/Google Sheets, PDF/Word, SQLite, CSV/JSON/XML, scheduling, email/text notifications, image manipulation, OCR, keyboard/mouse control, and TTS/speech recognition. A companion workbook and a video course accompany it.

results.name: markitdown
results.title: MarkItDown
results.summary: directly useful for converting PDFs, Excel, PPTX, and other docs to markdown for LLM pipelines; MIT, Microsoft-maintained

results.name: docling-mcp
results.title: Docling MCP
results.summary: MCP server for document conversion, processing, and generation via the Docling library — converts PDFs and other documents into structured DoclingDocument JSON with OCR, table structure detection, and image handling; supports local, remote (Docling Serve), and hybrid modes; RAG integrations with Milvus, LlamaIndex, and LlamaStack; LF AI & Data project from IBM Research Zurich, MIT, 730+ stars

results.name: seb-ocr
results.title: seb-ocr
results.summary: Vision-language pipeline for turning scanned historical pages into structured datasets — Gemini-based OCR with adaptive rate limiting, sliding-window entity extraction via Pydantic-constrained JSON, incremental caching, and semantic deduplication via embedding cosine similarity; single-script Python, MIT

results.name: rag-anything
results.title: RAG-Anything
results.summary: All-in-one multimodal RAG framework from HKU's Data Intelligence Lab, built on LightRAG — parses PDFs/Office/images/audio/video via MinerU, Docling, or PaddleOCR, then builds a multimodal knowledge graph linking text, tables, equations, and images; three query modes (text, VLM-enhanced, direct multimodal); 23,500+ GitHub stars; MIT

results.name: opendataloader-pdf
results.title: OpenDataLoader PDF
results.summary: Top-benchmarked open-source PDF parser with bounding boxes, formula extraction, and RAG-ready output — worth piloting for bioinformatics literature ingestion before committing.

results.name: pdf-mcp
results.title: pdf-mcp
results.summary: MCP server for surgical PDF access by AI agents — 13 tools for hybrid search (BM25 + semantic), selective page reading, table/image/chart extraction, OCR via Tesseract, corpus-wide multi-document search, and multi-column/CJK layout support; SQLite cache persists across restarts. MIT.

results.name: isaacflath-ocr-guides
results.title: Isaac Flath — Documents in AI Products (OCR Pipeline Guides)
results.summary: 14-post blog series covering OCR model selection, VLM OCR, speculative decoding, PDF retrieval, chunking, quantization, and document QA — practical guidelines for designing OCR pipelines

results.name: stirling-pdf
results.title: Stirling PDF
results.summary: Self-hosted REST API for 50+ PDF operations enables privacy-preserving agentic PDF workflows without external services

results.name: pullmd
results.title: PullMD
results.summary: Self-hosted anything-to-Markdown conversion service for AI agents — converts web pages (including Reddit/Hacker News threads with comment trees), PDFs, Office documents, EPUB, images, audio, and YouTube videos (transcripts with timecodes) into clean, boilerplate-stripped Markdown with metadata in YAML frontmatter; multi-strategy extraction (Cloudflare's Markdown endpoint plus parallel Readability/Trafilatura scored for quality); exposed via a PWA, REST API, MCP server, and a Claude Code skill; v3 added a markitdown document-conversion sidecar and an opt-in media tier for image captioning/audio transcription via any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; multi-arch Docker images; AGPL-3.0

results.name: parsebench
results.title: ParseBench
results.summary: LlamaIndex document parser benchmark — tests parsers across text, formatting, tables, charts, and page-location attribution; v1.0 with visual checks and scoring fixes (breaking change from v0.2)

results.name: meridian
results.title: Meridian
results.summary: GPU-accelerated document processing pipeline — Docling (8 load-balanced instances) for PDF layout detection, Qwen3-VL via vLLM for table/figure/formula reading, Ollama for embeddings, Qdrant for vector storage; stateless Celery workers on CPU calling long-lived GPU services over HTTP; measured at 118 pages/min on a single H200; includes text-only path (pypdfium2, 1000 docs/min on CPU); Apache-2.0

results.name: mineru
results.title: MinerU
results.summary: Open-source document parsing engine by OpenDataLab — converts PDFs, images, Office docs (Word/PPT/Excel), EPUB, OFD, HTML/MHTML, CSV into LLM-ready Markdown/JSON with four quality tiers (flash/basic/standard/advanced); VLM+OCR dual engine supporting 109 languages; local-first with optional remote API; CLI with agent-oriented continuation/locator system; local document library with search/watch/scan; MCP server; integrations with LangChain, RAGFlow, Dify, FastGPT; Python >=3.10; Apache-2.0 with commercial threshold (100M MAU or $20M revenue); ~80k stars

results.name: unstructured
results.title: Unstructured
results.summary: Open-source document ETL library — partitions 60+ file types (PDFs, Word, HTML, images, emails) into structured elements (Title, NarrativeText, Table, etc.) with layout ML enrichment, OCR, chunking, and embedding; connectors for 40+ sources/destinations; MCP server (Unstructured Transform) for agent-driven document processing; Apache-2.0, 15k+ stars

results.name: llama-index
results.title: LlamaIndex
results.summary: Open-source Python data framework for building LLM/RAG and document-agent apps: data connectors, indices/graphs, retrievers, and query engines to augment LLMs with private data, with 300+ integration packages (LLMs, embeddings, vector stores) on LlamaHub. Pairs with the commercial LlamaParse/Parse agentic-OCR platform. MIT.

results.name: five-levels-of-chunking
results.title: Five Levels of Chunking Strategies in RAG (Greg Kamradt's taxonomy)
results.summary: Taxonomy of RAG text-splitting strategies, from Greg Kamradt's '5 Levels of Text Splitting' (these are notes on that video): Level 1 fixed-size (character/sentence splitters), Level 2 recursive (hierarchical separators), Level 3 document/structure-based (respect headings, tables, code), Level 4 semantic (split at embedding-similarity breakpoints), Level 5 agentic (an LLM decides chunk boundaries from propositions). Higher levels trade cost/complexity for chunks that better match meaning; match the strategy to the data.

results.name: paperless-ngx
results.title: Paperless-ngx
results.summary: Mature self-hosted document management system — useful for archiving research docs but not an agent tool or developer library

results.name: reducto-model-routing
results.title: Reducto — When Is a Bigger Model Actually Better? (model routing framework)
results.summary: Reducto engineering-blog post (2026-08-13, Apurv Gandhi) framing document-model routing as a constrained optimization problem — a per-request 'model advantage' score (delta), a dimensionless cost-quality tradeoff parameter (lambda) that carries across model upgrades, an oracle frontier for benchmarking, and an AUC-based efficiency metric for grading a learned router against that oracle; reports 43.4%/56.6% split of low-gain vs. meaningful-gain requests across 8,276 paired evaluations.

results.name: pageindex
results.title: PageIndex
results.summary: Vectorless reasoning-based RAG engine — replaces vector index with hierarchical tree index, uses LLM reasoning for retrieval instead of similarity search; 98.7% accuracy on FinanceBench (vs vector RAG baselines); SDK with local mode (pip install pageindex) and cloud mode; ~$0.001/page indexing cost; ideal for financial/legal/medical/technical documents; MIT

results.name: crawl4ai
results.title: Crawl4AI
results.summary: Best-in-class async web-to-Markdown crawler for agent/RAG pipelines, but Docker API has had dense critical CVEs; library mode is safe to pilot

results.name: book-to-skill
results.title: Book to Skill
results.summary: directly useful for computational biology methods PDFs

results.name: vector-database-basics-hnsw
results.title: Vector Database Basics: HNSW (Tiger Data / Timescale)
results.summary: Tiger Data (Timescale) blog explainer on HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) vector indexing: describes HNSW's skip-list-inspired multi-layer graph (sparse long-edge upper layers for coarse navigation, dense lower layers for fine-grained search), and its use with pgvector/Timescale Vector on Postgres via the m (max connections per layer) and ef_construction (build-time candidate list size) parameters that trade index size/build time for search accuracy.

results.name: granola-cli

results.name: north-star-osint
results.title: North Star

results.name: mixpeek

Integrations include S3, GCS, R2, Mux, LangChain, and MCP. Catalog source is a Mixpeek education video contrasting an 'extract once, upstream of every app' model against a plain vector database.

results.name: pixelrag

results.name: blueprint4llm

results.name: scaledown-cdm

results.name: okf-agent-memory

results.name: agent-dispatcher
results.title: Agent Dispatcher — repository retrieval and specialist-role routing for Claude Code and Codex
results.summary: Claude Code plugin and Codex skill pack that routes a task to one of 27 specialist roles (engineering, design, testing, research, writing, operations) and assembles a bounded context packet of source excerpts using symbols, source text, code relationships, Git history, and stack-trace frames — rather than a full-repo dump. Ships 79 bundled local skills, references 31 external skills, 8 workflow recipes, a registry of 19 MCP servers, and 50 detection signals for role/skill selection. Standard retrieval runs locally with no model or network calls; optional features (model-assisted reranking, an external 'Jev' decision-engine API, an Onboarding Explorer, procedural learning from recorded outcomes) are off by default and require the operator's own provider configuration. Installs via `claude plugin marketplace add` + `claude plugin install` for Claude Code, or `python3 install_codex.py` for Codex (installs one skill to `~/.agents/skills/agent-dispatcher/`). Invoked with `/agent-dispatcher:agent-dispatcher <request>` (Claude) or `$agent-dispatcher <request>` (Codex); roles can be forced directly (e.g. `$agent-dispatcher reviewer`). Verification is explicit: each role defines what evidence counts as done and reports which checks ran, passed, or were left unverified. Requires Python 3.10+, Git, and an authenticated Claude Code or Codex; native Windows is unsupported (WSL recommended). MIT license, single maintainer, repo created 2026-09-19 with ~50 GitHub stars and 4 forks as of this review.

results.name: jantt

results.name: codex-workflow
results.title: Codex Workflow (viettran-edgeAI)
results.summary: Multi-agent orchestration architecture for Codex/Claude Code optimizing token usage within plan limits — 7 specialized roles (Main Agent, Companion/Luna, Investigator, Default Executor/Luna max, Senior Executor/Sol, Tester, Archivist) with fine-tuned batching, knowledge distribution via task-completion guides, and built-in per-agent token reporting; Sol xhigh ran 4h22m at 90% of 5h limit vs Astra at 260%; MIT

results.name: web-artifacts-builder
results.title: Web Artifacts Builder
results.summary: use when markdown isn't enough for interactive reports/dashboards

results.name: harnessx
results.title: HarnessX
results.summary: Python agent-harness foundry from the Darwin Agent Team separating model (ModelConfig) from behavior (HarnessConfig): a 9-dimension processor pipeline (context, control, evaluation, memory, multi-model, observability, tools, plus providers/plugins) composed with a `|` operator, plus two self-reported evolution loops — a meta-harness that auto-searches processor/config combinations, and RL fine-tuning (via VERL) on reward-annotated run trajectories. MIT-licensed, v0.1.0/Beta. Companion papers: HarnessX (arXiv:2606.14249) and a follow-on, DarwinX (arXiv:2608.07545).

results.name: open-knowledge-format
results.title: Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
results.summary: Google's spec (v0.2) for agent-friendly knowledge representation using Markdown + YAML frontmatter; adds provenance/freshness/trust signals, reference agent with web-crawling enrichment, interactive graph visualizer; closely aligned with our wiki pattern

results.name: claude-code-game-studios
results.title: Claude Code Game Studios
results.summary: Claude Code template that turns one session into a 49-agent, 74-skill simulated game studio with a three-tier director/lead/specialist hierarchy, 15 validation hooks, 14 path-scoped coding rules, and 62 document templates; ships engine-specific agent sets for Godot 4, Unity, and Unreal Engine 5; a project.yaml modes.rigor setting (minimal/standard/full) trades process weight for speed — the project's own measurement built four games from one brief and found the heavier standard-rigor build produced 30 process documents and lost a blind playtest ranking to the minimal-rigor build, which produced only a one-page brief; agents ask before acting and the user approves every write by default; MIT license.

results.name: qwen38-27b-200k-on-16gb
results.title: Qwen 3.8 27B at 200K Context on 16GB VRAM (tutorial)
results.summary: Practitioner recipe for running Qwen 3.8 27B UD-IQ4_XS at ~196K context and 50 t/s on a single RTX 5070 Ti (16GB) — prune non-ASCII rows from the embedding table and LM head (~700MB, ASCII-condensed variant published), offload the embedding table to CPU, disable MTP, use adaptive-KV streaming (llama.cpp fork) to page KV cache from host RAM, and quantize cache Q8 K / Q4 V

results.name: autoresearch
results.title: Autoresearch
results.summary: Highly influential autonomous experimentation loop pattern, but ML-training-specific — transferable idea, not transferable code

results.name: awesome-claude-code-subagents
results.title: Awesome Claude Code Subagents (VoltAgent)
results.summary: Curated collection of 161+ Claude Code subagent definitions across 10 categories (core dev, language specialists, infrastructure, quality/security, data/AI, developer experience, specialized domains, business/product, meta-orchestration, research/analysis); installable via Claude Code plugin marketplace, interactive shell script, or manual copy to ~/.claude/agents/; each subagent is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (name, description, tools, model); includes a /subagent-catalog skill for browsing and fetching agents; MIT, 6.4k stars

results.name: mcp-server-youtube-transcript
results.title: MCP Server YouTube Transcript
results.summary: MCP server exposing a single get_transcript tool for YouTube videos — language fallback, optional timestamps, ad-strip filtering, zero transcript-fetch dependencies; fills the YouTube-to-markdown gap for learning-vault capture

results.name: specship
results.title: SpecShip
results.summary: AWS spec-driven autonomous engineering framework (Kiro Power) — brownfield recon, contract-first markdown specs, strict TDD gates, adversarial parallel validation with up to 7 subagents, and self-healing fix agents

results.name: agent-skills-osmani
results.title: Agent Skills (Addy Osmani)
results.summary: Production-grade 24-skill engineering pack for AI coding agents — full SDLC lifecycle (define/plan/build/verify/review/ship) with anti-rationalization tables, verification gates, and 8 slash commands; 65K+ stars, Claude Code marketplace-installable, multi-platform (Cursor/Gemini/Windsurf/Copilot/Kiro); MIT

results.name: tldr-pages
results.title: tldr-pages
results.summary: Community-maintained simplified man pages — practical examples for common CLI commands; covers UNIX/Linux/macOS/FreeBSD/Windows/Android/Cisco IOS; official clients in Python, Rust (tlrc), and Node.js; web client with offline PWA; 40+ language translations; CC BY 4.0

results.name: awesome-a2a
results.title: Awesome A2A
results.summary: Curated ecosystem list for Google's Agent2Agent protocol — SDKs, framework integrations, community implementations, tools, and tutorials; use as discovery source for A2A-compatible agent infrastructure

results.name: get-shit-done
results.title: Get Shit Done (GSD)
results.summary: deprecated (moved to GSD Redux); superpowers skill system already covers meta-prompting and spec-driven development

results.name: claude-skills-rezvani
results.title: Claude Skills (Rezvani)
results.summary: 355-skill library for 13 AI coding tools — 18 domains (engineering, marketing, product, compliance, C-level advisory, research, finance, business ops), 602 stdlib-only Python CLI tools, 711 reference templates; cross-platform (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, and 7 more); MIT

results.name: nvk-llm-wiki
results.title: llm-wiki (nvk)
results.summary: Claude Code plugin (with ports for Codex, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, and generic SKILL.md agents) implementing Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern — treats raw sources as immutable "source code" and the LLM as a "compiler" that synthesizes them into a structured, source-linked wiki; organizes topics as isolated sub-wikis in a hub, runs parallel multi-agent research (5/8/10 agents per depth mode), and enforces that no wiki page exists without a cited source; commands include /wiki init, /wiki:research, /wiki:thesis, /wiki:query, /wiki:ingest, /wiki:compile; ~1.5k GitHub stars; MIT

results.name: fable-agent-orchestration
results.title: Fable Agent Orchestration
results.summary: Apache-2.0 skill database for multi-agent orchestration — 24 reusable skills covering worktree-isolated parallel PR workflows, two-critic review loops, agent PR validation against real diffs/CI, fake-green test detection, orphaned WIP recovery, instruction-drift control, behavior-contract harnesses, and phase-aware engineering ladders

results.name: taste-skill
results.title: Taste Skill
results.summary: Collection of portable SKILL.md files (design-taste-frontend and variants) that give AI coding agents layout/typography/motion/spacing guidance intended to reduce generic-looking generated UI, plus separate image-generation skills for design reference boards

results.name: skylos
results.title: Skylos
results.summary: Local-first static analysis CLI (Python, TS/JS, Java, Go, Kotlin, PHP, Rust, Dart, C#, Shell) that scans for dead code, security flaws, secrets, CI/CD misconfig, quality regressions, and AI-generated code defects; ships as CLI, GitHub Action, VS Code extension, and MCP server

results.name: ovis-vl-embedding
results.title: Ovis-VL-Embedding
results.summary: Omni-modal embedding model (2B and 9B variants) built on Qwen3.5 backbone — encodes text, images, visual documents, and video frames in a shared representation space; 77.46 overall on MMEB-v2 (78 datasets), 80.47 on visual document retrieval; no modality-specific projection heads, last-token hidden state as embedding; for multimodal RAG, cross-modal search, document retrieval

results.name: outlines
results.title: Outlines
results.summary: Structured generation library by .txt — guarantees LLM outputs conform to JSON Schema, Pydantic models, regex, grammars, or Python types via constrained decoding (FSM-based token masking); works with transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, OpenAI, Gemini; Jinja prompt templates, function calling inference, batch generation; Rust core (outlines-core) for performance; 65M+ downloads; trusted by NVIDIA, Cohere, HuggingFace, vLLM; Apache-2.0

results.name: documenso
results.title: Documenso
results.summary: Open-source DocuSign alternative for digital document signing — self-hostable TypeScript/React Router v7/Hono/Prisma stack with PDF signature support (@libpdf/core), i18n, Stripe billing, E2E tests (Playwright); Docker/K8s/Railway deployment; AGPL-3.0

results.name: grill-with-docs
results.title: Grill With Docs
results.summary: Well-structured DDD design-review skill that enforces domain language, but relies on companion format files (CONTEXT-FORMAT.md, ADR-FORMAT.md) not bundled with the skill.

results.name: model-workspace-protocol
results.title: Model Workspace Protocol (MWP)
results.summary: Research paper proposing filesystem structure as agent orchestration; numbered folders + markdown prompts replace multi-agent frameworks for sequential workflows

results.name: papermorph
results.title: Papermorph
results.summary: Agent skill (Claude Code / OpenCode, invoked as /papermorph) that turns a textbook PDF or a story into a self-hosted static web book — narrated step-by-step lessons with graded quizzes, paper-puppet picture-book films, or documentaries/shorts/explorable pages; plans chapters, writes narration, animates visuals to per-word TTS timing, and self-reviews output before publishing; exports to MP4+SRT or SCORM; MIT license (bundled MathJax Apache-2.0, media assets keep own licenses); ~1,000 GitHub stars

results.name: contextual-retrieval-anthropic
results.title: Contextual Retrieval (Anthropic Cookbook)
results.summary: Demonstrates three progressive techniques for improving RAG retrieval quality — contextual embeddings (situating each chunk within its source document before embedding), contextual BM25 hybrid search, and reranking — achieving up to 95.26% Pass@10

results.name: sdf
results.title: sdf
results.summary: Michael Fogleman's Python library for building 3D (and 2D) models from signed distance functions — primitives (sphere, box, torus, cylinder, cone, Platonic solids) composed with boolean ops (union, difference, intersection, including smooth/blended variants), transforms (translate, rotate, scale, twist, bend), and repetition (linear/circular arrays); meshes via Marching Cubes and exports STL natively plus 20+ formats (OBJ, PLY, ...) via meshio; also renders 2D SDFs from text/images for extrusion; actively maintained (pushed 2026-09-30); MIT.

results.name: diagram-design
results.title: Diagram Design
results.summary: Editorial-quality diagram skill for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Factory Droid, Pi, and other Agent Skills hosts — 42 visual types (architecture, flowchart, sequence, state, ER, timeline, Sankey, Wardley map, exploded axonometric, etc.) as self-contained HTML+SVG; brand onboarding from a URL; import from draw.io/Mermaid/Excalidraw; export to SVG/PNG; 9 semantic behavior patterns; optional accessible motion; 87 monochrome icons; no shadows, no Mermaid; MIT

results.name: hnswlib
results.title: HNSWlib
results.summary: Header-only C++ library (with Python bindings) implementing HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graph search — the standalone reference implementation of the HNSW algorithm by Yury Malkov and Dmitry Yashunin; incremental index construction, element deletion/update, custom C++ distances, L2/inner-product/cosine spaces; Apache-2.0
